meta.source: GiveWell, Research on Programs → Program reviews sheet
notes: Program names, GiveWell status and review dates come from the sheet.
description and givewell_view paraphrase the sheet. why_it_works is an editorial theory of change, not an evidence claim.
The four feedback attributes are an editorial classification.
evidence_* and cost_effectiveness_* stay null until copied from a GiveWell review page with its URL.
GiveWell content is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 US; keep attribution on the page.

interventions.name: Bridges to Prosperity footbridges
interventions.description: Footbridges in rural areas that connect isolated households to schools, clinics, and markets.
interventions.why_it_works: A bridge removes a physical barrier, so every trip to school, a clinic, or a market becomes shorter and safer.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 2: “Bridges to Prosperity footbridges”

interventions.name: Chlorine vouchers
interventions.description: Vouchers that households redeem for free chlorine to treat their drinking water.
interventions.why_it_works: The voucher removes the price of chlorine, which is one reason households do not treat water.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 3: “Chlorine vouchers”
Program reviews sheet, row 44: “Vouchers for water treatment” (merged here; status there: research ongoing)

interventions.name: Community-based household contact management programs for tuberculosis
interventions.description: Health workers visit the homes of people diagnosed with TB, screen close contacts, and give preventive medicine where appropriate.
interventions.why_it_works: People who share a home with a TB patient have high exposure, so the search starts where new cases are most likely.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 4: “Community-based household contact management programs for tuberculosis”

interventions.name: Community-based management of acute malnutrition
interventions.description: Outpatient identification and treatment of uncomplicated severe and moderate acute malnutrition.
interventions.why_it_works: Outpatient treatment is designed to reach more children than hospital care, because families do not have to stay at a hospital.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 5: “Community-based management of acute malnutrition”

interventions.name: Conditional cash transfers to increase infant vaccination as run by New Incentives
interventions.description: Cash to caregivers who bring infants for routine vaccinations, plus outreach and work to keep vaccines in stock at clinics.
interventions.why_it_works: Clinic visits cost caregivers time and money. A small payment at each visit offsets part of that cost.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 6: “Conditional cash transfers to increase infant vaccination as run by New Incentives”

interventions.name: Deworming (mass drug administration targeting schistosomiasis and/or soil-transmitted helminths)
interventions.description: Anti-parasitic drugs for all school-age children in at-risk areas, once or twice a year.
interventions.why_it_works: Where worm infections are common, treating everyone costs less than testing each child, and schools gather children in one place.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 7: “Deworming (mass drug administration targeting schistosomiasis and/or soil-transmitted helminths)”

interventions.name: Electronic immunization registry and mobile-based conditional cash transfers to increase vaccination as run by IRD Global
interventions.description: Conditional cash transfers through a mobile-phone platform to encourage infant immunization in low-coverage districts.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 8: “Electronic immunization registry and mobile-based conditional cash transfers to increase vaccination as run by IRD Global”

interventions.name: Eyeglasses to improve workers' manual dexterity
interventions.description: Free or subsidized eyeglasses for workers whose output depends on close manual work.
interventions.why_it_works: Near vision declines with age. Glasses let a worker keep doing precise work at full speed.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 9: “Eyeglasses to improve workers' manual dexterity”

interventions.name: Family planning radio campaigns
interventions.description: Radio campaigns that aim to increase the use of modern contraception.
interventions.why_it_works: One broadcast reaches many listeners at a very low cost per person.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 10: “Family planning radio campaigns”

interventions.name: Intermittent preventive treatment in infants (IPTi) for malaria
interventions.description: Preventive antimalarial medicine for young infants, given at routine vaccination visits.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 11: “Intermittent preventive treatment in infants (IPTi) for malaria”

interventions.name: Iron fortification
interventions.description: Iron added to staple foods, such as wheat flour, to reduce iron deficiency.
interventions.why_it_works: People eat staple foods every day, so fortification reaches them without any change in behavior.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 12: “Iron fortification”

interventions.name: Iron supplementation for school-age children
interventions.description: Iron supplements for school-age children to prevent anemia.
interventions.why_it_works: Schools give regular access to children, so a weekly supplement is easy to deliver.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 13: “Iron supplementation for school-age children”

interventions.name: Kangaroo mother care (KMC)
interventions.description: A low-cost alternative to neonatal intensive care for low-birthweight babies during their stay at a health facility.
interventions.why_it_works: Continuous skin-to-skin contact keeps a small baby warm and supports feeding when incubators are scarce.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 14: “Kangaroo mother care (KMC)”

interventions.name: Malaria vaccine
interventions.description: The RTS,S malaria vaccine for young children in moderate-to-high transmission areas, as part of wider malaria control.
interventions.why_it_works: The vaccine trains the immune system to attack the parasite early in an infection.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 15: “Malaria vaccine”

interventions.name: Mass distribution of long-lasting insecticide-treated nets
interventions.description: Long-lasting insecticide-treated nets for everyone in malaria-risk areas, usually every three years.
interventions.why_it_works: Malaria mosquitoes bite mostly at night. The net is a barrier, and the insecticide kills mosquitoes that land on it.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 16: “Mass distribution of long-lasting insecticide-treated nets”

interventions.name: One Acre Fund's tree program
interventions.description: Tree seedlings and training for small-scale farmers.
interventions.why_it_works: Trees are a slow-growing asset. Farmers can later sell the timber or use it themselves.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 17: “One Acre Fund's tree program”

interventions.name: Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) and zinc supplementation
interventions.description: Treatment of dehydration from diarrhea with a glucose-and-salt solution, plus a short course of zinc.
interventions.why_it_works: Diarrhea kills mainly through dehydration. ORS replaces the lost fluid and salts.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 18: “Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) and zinc supplementation”

interventions.name: Participatory Learning and Action - Maternal and Neonatal Health
interventions.description: Facilitated groups of women, especially pregnant women, who develop local plans to improve care-seeking and prevention for mothers and newborns.
interventions.why_it_works: The group finds its own local problems and solutions, which can make the changes easier to keep.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 19: “Participatory Learning and Action - Maternal and Neonatal Health”

interventions.name: Ponseti casting for clubfoot
interventions.description: Treatment for clubfoot: a series of casts to correct the foot, a small tendon procedure, and then bracing.
interventions.why_it_works: Early correction lets a child walk normally and prevents a lifelong disability.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 20: “Ponseti casting for clubfoot”

interventions.name: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention
interventions.description: Monthly courses of antimalarial medicine for children under 5 during the peak transmission season.
interventions.why_it_works: Where malaria is concentrated in a few months each year, drugs given only in that window protect children when risk is highest.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 21: “Seasonal malaria chemoprevention”

interventions.name: SMS reminders for immunization
interventions.description: Text messages that remind caregivers of their children's upcoming vaccination dates.
interventions.why_it_works: Many caregivers intend to vaccinate but forget the date. A reminder at the right time costs very little.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 22: “SMS reminders for immunization”

interventions.name: Syphilis screening and treatment during pregnancy
interventions.description: Rapid point-of-care syphilis testing and treatment during pregnancy.
interventions.why_it_works: Treatment during pregnancy prevents transmission to the baby, so a cheap test at the first visit protects two people.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 23: “Syphilis screening and treatment during pregnancy”

interventions.name: Vitamin A supplementation
interventions.description: High-dose vitamin A for children aged about 6 months to 5 years in high-risk areas, two or three times a year.
interventions.why_it_works: Vitamin A deficiency weakens the immune system. A periodic high dose tops up a child's stores.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 24: “Vitamin A supplementation”

interventions.name: Water quality interventions
interventions.description: Removal or disabling of pathogens in water, for example with chlorine dispensers or in-line chlorination.
interventions.why_it_works: Treatment at the water source protects everyone who collects water there, without effort from each household.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 25: “Water quality interventions”

interventions.name: Family planning commodities
interventions.description: Distribution of family planning commodities.
interventions.why_it_works: Stockouts mean that women who want contraception cannot get it. A reliable supply closes that gap.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 26: “Family planning commodities”

interventions.name: Breastfeeding promotion
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell calls the program promising and may look for funding opportunities in some contexts.
interventions.description: Counseling, community work, and media that encourage mothers to breastfeed exclusively and for longer.
interventions.why_it_works: Breast milk gives nutrition and protection from infection, and clean water is not necessary.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 28: “Breastfeeding promotion”

interventions.name: Cash transfers
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell supported GiveDirectly from 2012 to 2022 and updated its assessment in 2024; it is now funding scoping of program variations.
interventions.description: Cash grants to poor people in low-income countries.
interventions.why_it_works: Households know their own needs. Cash lets them buy, invest, or repay what matters most to them.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 29: “Cash transfers”

interventions.name: Chlorhexidine for umbilical cord care
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell finds it promising in some circumstances and plans more research.
interventions.description: An antiseptic applied to the newborn's umbilical cord stump to prevent infection.
interventions.why_it_works: The cord stump is an open route for bacteria in the first days of life. An antiseptic closes that route.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 30: “Chlorhexidine for umbilical cord care”

interventions.name: Community-based intervention packages to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell still wants to find a promising program of this type.
interventions.description: Care for women and newborns through community outreach workers, such as warmth after birth, breastfeeding help, vitamin K, and referrals.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 31: “Community-based intervention packages to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality”

interventions.name: Facility-based maternal and neonatal health interventions
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell finds it promising but is highly uncertain about specific programs, so it may attach an evaluation to any grant.
interventions.description: Training for health workers to deliver a package of care during and after birth in health facilities.
interventions.why_it_works: Many deaths happen around birth. Better-trained staff at that moment can act on complications fast.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 32: “Facility-based maternal and neonatal health interventions”

interventions.name: Mass distribution of azithromycin to reduce child mortality
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell's review found it may be cost-effective enough, but it is studying implementation and the risk of antibiotic resistance.
interventions.description: An antibiotic given to all children in an age range, once or twice a year.
interventions.why_it_works: A mass dose clears many common infections at once, including ones that are not yet diagnosed.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 33: “Mass distribution of azithromycin to reduce child mortality”

interventions.name: Probiotic supplementation for preterm newborns
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell finds it promising and wants to learn about implementation opportunities.
interventions.description: Probiotic supplements for small or preterm newborns to prevent necrotizing enterocolitis and sepsis.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 34: “Probiotic supplementation for preterm newborns”

interventions.name: Sayana® Press
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell finds it promising and plans more research.
interventions.description: An injectable contraceptive in a prefilled single-use device that community health workers or women themselves can give.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 35: “Sayana® Press”

interventions.name: Targeting the Ultra Poor
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell continues to look for programs of this type that are cost-effective and need funding.
interventions.description: Productive assets such as livestock for very poor households, with mentoring, training, and other support.
interventions.why_it_works: Very poor households often face several constraints at once. The bundle tries to relax all of them together.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 36: “Targeting the Ultra Poor”

interventions.name: Attractive toxic sugar baits for malaria control
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized for lack of evidence; GiveWell expects new evidence.
interventions.description: Sugar mixed with a substance lethal to mosquitoes, used to reduce mosquito populations.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 37: “Attractive toxic sugar baits for malaria control”

interventions.name: Community health promoters as run by Living Goods
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell will revisit when results of a larger-scale trial are available.
interventions.description: Promoters who sell health and household goods door to door and give basic health advice.
interventions.why_it_works: A local promoter lowers the distance to basic care and products, and sales help pay for the work.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 38: “Community health promoters as run by Living Goods”

interventions.name: Community salt substitution
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell's best guess is that it is below its funding bar; it will revisit when a stroke study is published.
interventions.description: Table salt replaced for a whole community by a substitute in which potassium chloride replaces part of the sodium.
interventions.why_it_works: Less sodium and more potassium lower blood pressure, and people do not have to change what they cook.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 39: “Community salt substitution”

interventions.name: Eave tubes to control malaria
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized for lack of evidence; GiveWell expects new evidence.
interventions.description: Tubes with insecticide-treated netting installed in the gap between roof and walls to kill mosquitoes as they pass.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 40: “Eave tubes to control malaria”

interventions.name: Educate! Experience program
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized for lack of evidence; GiveWell expects new evidence.
interventions.description: Mentoring for students in their last two years of secondary school, with a focus on leadership, work readiness, and entrepreneurship.
interventions.why_it_works: Skills that school often does not teach may help young people find work or start a business.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 41: “Educate! Experience program”

interventions.name: Electronic partogram
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized for lack of evidence; GiveWell expects new evidence.
interventions.description: Help for health facilities to move from paper to electronic partograms to track and manage labor.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 42: “Electronic partogram”

interventions.name: HPV vaccination to prevent cervical cancer
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell believed in 2020 that there were probably no large funding gaps, because vaccine supply was the constraint.
interventions.description: HPV vaccination for girls aged 9 to 14 to prevent cervical cancer.
interventions.why_it_works: Vaccination before exposure prevents the infection that causes most cervical cancer.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 43: “HPV vaccination to prevent cervical cancer”

interventions.name: Antenatal corticosteroids for pregnant women at risk of preterm birth
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized because trial results differ and harm is possible; GiveWell awaits an ongoing trial.
interventions.description: Corticosteroids for women at 24 to 34 weeks of pregnancy who are at risk of preterm birth.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 45: “Antenatal corticosteroids for pregnant women at risk of preterm birth”

interventions.name: Antiretroviral therapy to treat HIV/AIDS
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell's best guess is that it is below its cost-effectiveness bar.
interventions.description: Ongoing antiretroviral drugs for people living with HIV to reduce illness and extend life.
interventions.why_it_works: The drugs suppress the virus, which keeps the immune system working.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 46: “Antiretroviral therapy to treat HIV/AIDS”

interventions.name: Artemisia tea
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized after a shallow look at the evidence.
interventions.description: Malaria treatment with a tea made from Artemisia plants.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 47: “Artemisia tea”

interventions.name: Aspirin for cardiovascular disease prevention
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on a shallow cost-effectiveness estimate and few visible funding opportunities.
interventions.description: Aspirin for people at risk of cardiovascular disease, to reduce heart attacks and strokes.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 48: “Aspirin for cardiovascular disease prevention”

interventions.name: Bracelets for immunization
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on cost-effectiveness and on thin evidence outside the original setting.
interventions.description: Colored bracelets for infants that show immunization status, as a social signal.
interventions.why_it_works: A visible bracelet reminds parents of the next dose and shows neighbors who is up to date.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 49: “Bracelets for immunization”

interventions.name: Bt eggplant adoption
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on a shallow cost-effectiveness estimate and limited room for funding.
interventions.description: Support for farmers to adopt eggplant that is genetically modified to be toxic to a major pest.
interventions.why_it_works: A crop that resists its main pest needs less spraying and loses less of the harvest.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 50: “Bt eggplant adoption”

interventions.name: Cataract surgery
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell could not find strong evidence that charity activity increases the number of surgeries.
interventions.description: Surgery that removes a clouded eye lens and replaces it with an artificial lens.
interventions.why_it_works: A short operation can restore sight that would otherwise be lost for life.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 51: “Cataract surgery”

interventions.name: Clean cookstoves
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized after GiveWell assessed the evidence of effectiveness.
interventions.description: Stoves designed to reduce indoor smoke compared with open fires that burn wood or dung.
interventions.why_it_works: Less smoke in the home means less exposure to air pollution for the people who cook and the children near them.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 52: “Clean cookstoves”

interventions.name: Community distribution of polypill for cardiovascular disease prevention
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on a shallow cost-effectiveness estimate.
interventions.description: One pill with fixed doses of several drugs to reduce cardiovascular risk, distributed in the community.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 53: “Community distribution of polypill for cardiovascular disease prevention”

interventions.name: Community-based antibiotic delivery for possible serious bacterial infection (PSBI) management
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized because evidence on community delivery alone is lacking.
interventions.description: Home-based antibiotics for newborns with suspected serious infection when a hospital referral is not possible.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 54: “Community-based antibiotic delivery for possible serious bacterial infection (PSBI) management”

interventions.name: Conditional subsidies for seasonal labor migration in northern Bangladesh
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell supported this from 2014 to 2019, then deprioritized it after newer evidence.
interventions.description: Cash or interest-free loans that help rural workers migrate for work during the lean season.
interventions.why_it_works: In the lean season there is little local work. A small subsidy covers the risk and the fare of a trip to find jobs elsewhere.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 55: “Conditional subsidies for seasonal labor migration in northern Bangladesh”

interventions.name: Condom promotion and distribution to prevent HIV/AIDS
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized after GiveWell assessed the evidence of effectiveness.
interventions.description: Education and advertising for condom use, and free or subsidized condoms.
interventions.why_it_works: Condoms block transmission, so easier access can reduce new infections.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 56: “Condom promotion and distribution to prevent HIV/AIDS”

interventions.name: Cryptococcal antigen testing for people living with HIV
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized because cost-effective room for funding seems lacking.
interventions.description: Diagnosis and treatment of a deadly fungal infection, mainly among people living with HIV.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 57: “Cryptococcal antigen testing for people living with HIV”

interventions.name: Deworming pregnant people
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized because GiveWell expects few funding opportunities.
interventions.description: A single preventive deworming dose for pregnant people to reduce infections that contribute to anemia.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 58: “Deworming pregnant people”

interventions.name: Diagnosis and treatment for chronic pulmonary aspergillosis
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on limited evidence in low-resource settings and hard implementation.
interventions.description: Diagnosis and treatment of a deadly fungal infection, mainly among people with structural lung disease.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 59: “Diagnosis and treatment for chronic pulmonary aspergillosis”

interventions.name: Diagnosis and treatment for disseminated histoplasmosis
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on shallow cost-effectiveness and funding-room estimates.
interventions.description: Diagnosis and treatment of a deadly fungal infection, mainly among people living with HIV.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 60: “Diagnosis and treatment for disseminated histoplasmosis”

interventions.name: Diagnosis and treatment for pneumocystis pneumonia
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on a shallow look at evidence and cost-effectiveness.
interventions.description: Diagnosis and treatment of a deadly fungal infection, mainly among people living with HIV.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 61: “Diagnosis and treatment for pneumocystis pneumonia”

interventions.name: Distribution of eyeglasses to improve academic performance
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on the evidence; GiveWell rates the evidence for glasses for workers more highly.
interventions.description: Free or subsidized glasses for students with poor vision, to improve school performance.
interventions.why_it_works: A child who cannot see the board cannot learn from it.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 62: “Distribution of eyeglasses to improve academic performance”

interventions.name: Early childhood psychosocial stimulation
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on evidence and cost-effectiveness.
interventions.description: Training for parents to support development through play and other activities, to build cognitive and language skills.
interventions.why_it_works: The brain develops fastest in the first years, so small changes in daily play can have large effects.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 63: “Early childhood psychosocial stimulation”

interventions.name: Education in developing countries
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized as a category on the evidence; GiveWell may look at single education programs later.
interventions.description: A wide range of programs that aim to improve education.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 64: “Education in developing countries”

interventions.name: Eggs for complementary feeding
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on a shallow cost-effectiveness estimate.
interventions.description: Chicken eggs given to families to feed to infants alongside breast milk.
interventions.why_it_works: Eggs are a compact source of protein and micronutrients at the age when growth falters.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 65: “Eggs for complementary feeding”

interventions.name: Generic hepatitis C medication
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on a shallow cost-effectiveness estimate.
interventions.description: Generic direct-acting antivirals to treat hepatitis C.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 66: “Generic hepatitis C medication”

interventions.name: Immunization to prevent meningitis A
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on room for more funding.
interventions.description: Immunization campaigns against meningitis A to prevent deaths, brain damage, and hearing loss.
interventions.why_it_works: Campaigns vaccinate many people at once and can stop a disease that spreads in epidemics.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 67: “Immunization to prevent meningitis A”

interventions.name: Integrated community case management
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized after GiveWell assessed the evidence of effectiveness.
interventions.description: Community health workers trained and supplied to treat simple pneumonia, malaria, and diarrhea.
interventions.why_it_works: Treatment close to home comes sooner, and these illnesses kill quickly when treatment is late.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 68: “Integrated community case management”

interventions.name: Intermittent preventive treatment of malaria during pregnancy
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell found low cost-effectiveness and weak evidence.
interventions.description: Antimalarial drugs for at-risk pregnant women in the second and third trimesters.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 69: “Intermittent preventive treatment of malaria during pregnancy”

interventions.name: Interventions to promote handwashing
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on evidence and cost-effectiveness.
interventions.description: Education and/or materials such as soap to promote handwashing.
interventions.why_it_works: Soap removes pathogens from hands before they reach food or mouths.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 70: “Interventions to promote handwashing”

interventions.name: Larval source management for malaria control
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized for lack of evidence; GiveWell expects new evidence.
interventions.description: Methods that kill mosquitoes at the larval stage, such as habitat changes, larvicide on water, and biological control.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 71: “Larval source management for malaria control”

interventions.name: Lymphoedema management to prevent acute adenolymphangitis in podoconiosis
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on a shallow cost-effectiveness estimate.
interventions.description: Education and supplies such as bandages and shoes for people with podoconiosis, to reduce acute attacks.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 72: “Lymphoedema management to prevent acute adenolymphangitis in podoconiosis”

interventions.name: Magnesium sulfate for preeclampsia
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell thinks broad programs are likely below its cost-effectiveness range.
interventions.description: Wider availability of magnesium sulfate to prevent eclampsia in people with severe preeclampsia.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 73: “Magnesium sulfate for preeclampsia”

interventions.name: Malaria rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs)
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized for lack of evidence that the tests reduce deaths.
interventions.description: Rapid tests to reduce overprescription of antimalarials and to find other causes of fever.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 74: “Malaria rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs)”

interventions.name: Manual water pumps for farming households
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on a shallow cost-effectiveness estimate.
interventions.description: Manual pumps for smallholder farmers to irrigate crops when rainfall is low.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 75: “Manual water pumps for farming households”

interventions.name: Mass media to promote behavior change as run by Development Media International
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell sees limited evidence, based on a trial of the child-mortality program.
interventions.description: Radio and television programs that encourage better health practices.
interventions.why_it_works: One broadcast reaches a whole region at a very low cost per listener.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 76: “Mass media to promote behavior change as run by Development Media International”

interventions.name: Mass screen-and-treatment programs for tuberculosis
interventions.givewell_view: GiveWell's best guess is below its bar, but it is uncertain about costs, feasibility, and differences by place.
interventions.description: TB testing for everyone above an age threshold, and treatment for people with the disease.
interventions.why_it_works: Many people with TB do not know they have it. Finding them early stops them infecting others.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 77: “Mass screen-and-treatment programs for tuberculosis”

interventions.name: Microfinance
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized after GiveWell assessed the evidence of effectiveness.
interventions.description: Loans and other financial services, such as savings or insurance, for poor people.
interventions.why_it_works: The theory: small businesses have high returns to capital but cannot borrow from banks.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 78: “Microfinance”

interventions.name: Micronutrient powders
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on a shallow cost-effectiveness estimate.
interventions.description: Packets of vitamins and minerals that families add to children's food.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 79: “Micronutrient powders”

interventions.name: Neonatal vitamin A supplementation (NVAS)
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on evidence and limited room for funding.
interventions.description: A large dose of vitamin A for infants shortly after birth.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 80: “Neonatal vitamin A supplementation (NVAS)”

interventions.name: Non-pneumatic anti-shock garments
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on room for more funding.
interventions.description: A compression garment that stabilizes women with postpartum hemorrhage until they get treatment.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 81: “Non-pneumatic anti-shock garments”

interventions.name: Oral ivermectin mass drug administration for scabies control
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on cost-effectiveness and room for funding.
interventions.description: Oral ivermectin for almost everyone in a scabies-affected community.
interventions.why_it_works: Scabies spreads by close contact, so everyone is treated at once to stop reinfection.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 82: “Oral ivermectin mass drug administration for scabies control”

interventions.name: Oral Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on cost-effectiveness.
interventions.description: Antiretroviral drugs for HIV-negative people to prevent infection.
interventions.why_it_works: The drugs block the virus before it can take hold.

sources.title: Program reviews sheet, row 83: “Oral Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV”

interventions.name: Polio eradication activities
interventions.givewell_view: Deprioritized on a shallow cost-effectiveness estimate.
interventions.description: Support for polio vaccination in endemic countries and related work elsewhere.
interventions.why_it_works: If transmission stops everywhere, the disease is gone and no future vaccination is necessary.

interventions.name: Post-discharge malaria chemoprevention (PDMC) for children with severe anemia
